question.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 & 12 \\ 12 & 13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}13-\lambda  & 12 \\ 12 & 13-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (13-\lambda )(13-\lambda )-144 & =0 \\ 169-26\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-144 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-26\lambda +25 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda -25) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =25,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{25}=5 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$
